correctness.rationale: Under infinite Bernoulli exchangeability, de Finetti reduces the event to E f(Theta), f(t)=4t³−3t⁴ with ETheta=mu, ETheta²=nu and mu²<=nu<=mu. For upper low-nu, the quadratic majorant satisfies q−f=3(t−a)²(t−b)² where a+b=2/3, ab=2mu/3−nu and a<=mu<=b; the two-atom support attains equality. For upper high-nu, q−f=3t(t−b)²(t−c) with b=nu/mu>=2/3 and c=4/3−2b<=0; support 0,b attains. For lower low-nu, f−q=3t(t−b)²(c−t) with b<=1/6 and c>=1; support 0,b attains. For middle lower phase, f−q=3(t−a)²(1−t)(t−c), a=(mu−nu)/(1−mu)>=1/6 and c=1/3−2a<=0, attained at a,1. For final lower phase, f−(13t²−t)/12=3t(1−t)(t−1/6)² and support 0,1/6,1 with weights (1−7mu+6nu,36(mu−nu)/5,(6nu−mu)/5) matches both moments and is nonnegative under the stated branch conditions. Boundary contacts agree, mu=0,1 and nu=mu²,mu collapse correctly; mixing the endpoint directing laws realizes every intermediate probability. These are full-domain analytic inequalities, not an inference from numerical tests.
residual_risks: The independent finite symbolic/rational checks do not constitute a proof over all real moment pairs; universal correctness comes from the polynomial factorizations, feasibility inequalities, and exact support measures.
The result applies ONLY to infinite exchangeability and exactly fixed first TWO moments; it is false as a universal bound over all four-fold exchangeable distributions.

value.rationale: The 3-of-4 reliability/predictive-success probability is a natural fixed-horizon statistic whose value is not determined by marginal and pairwise frequencies even under de Finetti extendibility. The theorem solves that concrete partial-identification problem completely, with sharp five algebraic phases, a nontrivial universal 1/6 contact support, explicit attainability, and numerical differences from finite exchangeability. Knowing the exact interval can be needed when forecasts or systems report only one- and two-coordinate success rates. This is a motivated exact invariant of a natural class, not an arbitrary one-off slice or code-only experiment. It neither claims new moment-problem duality nor a general all-threshold classification.
residual_risks: The scope is only one finite horizon and threshold, not all n,k or empirical estimation of the moments.
If future literature confirms prior exact coverage of these phase formulas, the independent value assessment would need revision in light of that coverage.

limitations: The universal proof depends on infinitely extendible Bernoulli data and exact two fixed latent moments, not finite four-fold exchangeability or estimated population moments.
